about: The rule spec both local readers of a project folder follow: Eternia's (Dart, lib/core/io/project_folder_reader.dart) and hermes' (Python, agent_runtime/project_files/). Plan docs/embedded_hermes/planned/PHONE_PROJECT_FOLDERS_FILE_TREE_2026-11-21.md section 6. Each reader keeps these values as constants and a test pins them to this file; the cases in cases/*.json run on both readers.

path_grammar.rule: A request path is root-relative, '/'-separated and case-exact. It is never empty, never starts with '/', holds no '\\', no control character (U+0000-U+001F, U+007F), no empty, '.' or '..' segment, and its first segment is not a drive letter ('C:'). An absent path means the root itself.

confinement.rule: A path is resolved through every symlink before it is used; a resolved path outside the canonical root is refused 'outside_root'. While listing or searching, a symlink is listed with kind 'link' and never followed, wherever it points. A revoked grant or a stale bookmark refuses 'grant_revoked' and never falls back to a wider path.

ignore.gitignore: Only the root's .gitignore is honoured, when listing and searching (a read by explicit path is not refused for it). A line is trimmed of trailing spaces; a blank line or one starting with '#' is skipped; a line starting with '!' is not honoured (negation is a documented edge case, not worked). A trailing '/' matches directories only. A pattern holding a '/' (other than a trailing one) is anchored at the root, a leading '/' dropped; otherwise it matches an entry's name at any depth. '**/' matches any run of leading directories, a trailing '/**' everything inside, '*' any run of characters but '/', '?' one character but '/'; every other character, '[' included, is literal.
ignore.applies: The skip list and .gitignore apply to entries met while walking (tree, grep). '.git' is never listed, searched or read, by any path, through a symlink or not.

size_and_type.rule: A file whose first binary_probe_bytes hold a NUL byte is binary: listed with its size, refused 'binary' as text and skipped by grep. Text is UTF-8, decoded strictly: undecodable bytes are refused 'not_text', never replaced. A file over max_read_bytes is refused 'too_large' and skipped by grep.

arguments.path: a directory, absent for the root

tree.reply: {path, entries, total, offset, next?}: path is the listed directory ('' for the root); entries are pre-order, each directory's children sorted by name, a file as {path, kind: 'file', size}, a directory as {path, kind: 'dir'} followed by its own entries while within depth, a symlink as {path, kind: 'link'}; at most max_entries from offset; next is present while entries remain.

read.reply: {path, size, chars, offset, content, next?}: size in bytes, chars the text's length in Unicode code points, content at most page_code_points code points from offset; next is present while text remains.

arguments.path: a directory, absent for the root

grep.reply: {pattern, path, matches, total, offset, next?}: every text file under path in tree order, its lines split on '\n' with one trailing '\r' dropped; a match is {path, line (1-based), text (the line's first line_code_points code points)}; at most max_matches from offset.

refusals.outside_root: the path resolves outside the root (a symlink out of it)
refusals.ignored: the path is inside .git, which is never listed or read
refusals.not_a_directory: tree or grep named a file
refusals.bad_argument: depth, offset or pattern is out of bounds
refusals.grant_revoked: a granted folder's grant or bookmark no longer holds
refusals.virtual_root_read_only: a write sent to a reader of a virtual root
